text:
"Palmieri stoned by Kuemper twice. Been that kind of start to season for Palmieri," NHL.com's Stefen Rosner posted on Friday, and that is the season in two sentences. Kyle Palmieri has three goals on 5.9 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and none in his last seven games despite 2.9 expected over that stretch.

The looks are there. He's producing 1.18 expected goals per 60, above where he was last season, and the Islanders take 54% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on the ice, six points better than without him. He's shooting 7.9% when our range for him centers near 12%. Five points in 18 games is a finishing slump, not a decline.

At 35, back from the torn ACL that ended his 2025-26 after 25 games, he's playing 17:28 a night lately, up 1.6 minutes, which says the coaching staff sees the same process we do. The one gap worth noting: no power-play points yet. The Smithtown native has 276 career goals, and the shots he's getting are the kind that usually add to it.
